scope: Theorem 6.2 (A small critical trajectory) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE₃ Universality for the Weak Random-Bond Ising Model” (preprints/Quenched-SLE3-Universality-for-the-Weak-Random-Bond-Ising-Model-October-5-2026/quenched-sle3-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dbf1578546653fc5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the scale-step parameters chosen in Proposition 4.1 and a sufficiently large initial spacing s0. There are constants A, B, D, c > 0, a fixed cutoff H, and θ0 > 0 such that, for each 0 < θ < θ0, one can choose a deterministic h = h(θ) = O(θ2) with the following property. The iterates at spacings sk = s0Lk satisfy, with vk = vH,k, vk > 0, Xk ≤ A √ vk, Yk ≤ Bvk, |mk| ≤ Dvk, (6.4) and vk ≤ 1 v−1 0 + ck . (6.5) In particular Xk, Yk, mk → 0. Their uniform bounds over all k can be made arbitrarily small by decreasing θ0.
